# pocketid_api (Resource)

Manages an [API](https://pocket-id.org/docs/guides/apis) in Pocket-ID: a resource server that OIDC clients can request access tokens for, with the permissions a token can carry. A client asks for a token for an API with the `resource` parameter of its token request, and the token's `aud` is the API's `resource` and its `scope` the permissions the client is granted. Which clients may request which permissions is set with `pocketid_api_client_access`.

Pocket-ID replaces the permissions of an API as a whole and matches them by key, so they are an attribute of the API here, not a resource of their own.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An API with two permissions. A client asks for a token for the API with
# resource=https://api.orders.example.com and scope=read:orders.
resource "pocketid_api" "orders" {
  name     = "Orders API"
  resource = "https://api.orders.example.com"

  # Setting permissions replaces all of them. The map key is the permission key,
  # the scope a client requests.
  permissions = {
    "read:orders" = {
      name        = "Read orders"
      description = "Read the orders of the signed-in user"
    }
    "write:orders" = {
      name = "Write orders"
    }
  }
}

# Allow every client registered through a Client ID Metadata Document to use the
# API on behalf of a user, limited to the permissions marked here.
resource "pocketid_api" "catalog" {
  name               = "Catalog API"
  resource           = "https://api.catalog.example.com"
  allow_cimd_clients = true

  permissions = {
    "read:catalog" = {
      name                     = "Read the catalog"
      allowed_for_cimd_clients = true
    }
    "write:catalog" = {
      name = "Write the catalog"
    }
  }
}

# Client access refers to permissions by ID.
output "read_orders_permission_id" {
  value = pocketid_api.orders.permissions["read:orders"].id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The friendly name of the API.
- `resource` (String) The resource identifier of the API, usually a URL such as `https://api.example.com`. It need not be a page that exists. It is the `resource` of a token request and the `aud` of the token. Pocket-ID cannot change it, so changing it replaces the API, and with it every permission and client access. It must not end with a slash: Pocket-ID stores the resource without trailing slashes.

### Optional

- `allow_cimd_clients` (Boolean) Whether every client registered through a [Client ID Metadata Document](https://pocket-id.org/docs/guides/client-id-metadata-documents) may use the API on behalf of a user, limited to the permissions with `allowed_for_cimd_clients`. It covers current and future metadata-document clients, and never client access (M2M), because these clients are public. Defaults to false.
- `permissions` (Attributes Map) The permissions of the API, by key. The key is what a client puts in the `scope` of a token request, such as `read:orders`. Setting this attribute replaces all permissions of the API: a permission that is left out is deleted, with every client's access to it. Pocket-ID rejects keys with characters that are not valid in an OAuth scope, and the reserved keys `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `email_verified`, `groups` and `offline_access`. Defaults to none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the API.

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Required:

- `name` (String) The friendly name of the permission, shown to users when they are asked to consent.

Optional:

- `allowed_for_cimd_clients` (Boolean) Whether metadata-document clients may request the permission when `allow_cimd_clients` is on. Pocket-ID keeps the selection while `allow_cimd_clients` is off. Defaults to false.
- `description` (String) What the permission allows.

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The ID of the permission. Client access refers to permissions by this ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An API is imported with its ID, the `id` that GET /api/apis returns for it.
terraform import pocketid_api.orders <api_id>
```
